newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua lowers coffee harvest, export outlook.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua lowers coffee harvest, export outlook.

text.p: Nicaragua's coffee growers said Tuesday the country will produce 950,000 quintales (100-lb bags) of coffee in its 1996-97 cycle, a slight drop from the 1.0 million quintales projected earlier this month.

Top members of Nicaraguan Union of Coffee Growers (Unicafe) told a news conference that with 85 percent of this year's harvest in, projected exports from the cycle have fallen as well from 850,000 to 800,000 quintales.

At the start of the coffee harvest in November, Nicaragua had expected to produce more than 1.2 million quintales, but a lack of financing to fertilize crops, bad roads, armed gangs and a bout with leaf rust (La Roya) have hurt production, Unicafe co-presidents Amilcar Navarro and Eduardo Rizo said.

Rizo said Unicafe's board of directors will meet next Monday to discuss the body's restructuration and modernization, and later in the week would meet with the economic cabinet of Nicaragua's new government to present coffee grower demands.
Right-wing President Arnoldo Aleman, himself a coffee grower, took power in Nicaragua on Jan 10.
Navarro said Unicafe will ask the government to restructure coffee growers' debts with Nicaragua's state banks and have these state banks give credit to indebted growers.
